topics.title: Program Structure, Variables & Types
topics.summary: Learn how a C# program is organized and how the compiler uses types to catch many mistakes before the program runs.

concepts.name: Strong typing
concepts.explanation: Every expression has a type. The compiler checks assignments, method calls, operators, and conversions so incompatible operations can be caught at compile time.

concepts.name: Built-in types
concepts.explanation: Common types include int, long, float, double, decimal, bool, char, string, and object. Choose a type based on the data and operations you need, not only on size.

concepts.name: Variables and constants
concepts.explanation: Declare local variables with an explicit type or var when the initializer makes the type clear. const is for compile-time constants; readonly is a separate field concept learned later.

topics.challenge: Declare a string, an int, and a bool, calculate whether the score passes 80, and print the values.
topics.hint: C# statements normally end with semicolons. Keep the comparison result in a bool variable.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#

topics.title: Operators, Conditions & Switch
topics.summary: Build expressions and select behavior with if/else, comparison and boolean operators, conditional expressions, and switch.

concepts.name: Operators
concepts.explanation: Arithmetic, comparison, equality, and logical operators combine typed values. C# distinguishes boolean logic from bitwise operations even though some operator symbols overlap.

concepts.name: if/else
concepts.explanation: if requires a bool condition; C# does not treat arbitrary numbers or strings as truthy/falsy.

concepts.name: switch
concepts.explanation: switch statements and switch expressions are useful when behavior depends on discrete cases. Modern patterns can test values, types, properties, and ranges.

topics.challenge: Write an if/else that checks an integer score against 80 and also assign a text result with a switch expression.
topics.hint: For the switch expression, put the catch-all discard pattern _ last.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#

topics.title: Loops, Arrays & Lists
topics.summary: Repeat work with for/while/foreach and store ordered data in arrays and generic List<T> collections.

concepts.name: Arrays
concepts.explanation: Arrays have a fixed length after creation and use zero-based indexing. They are efficient when the number of slots is known.

concepts.name: List<T>
concepts.explanation: List<T> is a resizable generic collection. Add, Remove, Count, indexing, and enumeration cover many everyday collection tasks.

concepts.name: Loop choice
concepts.explanation: Use foreach when you only need each item, for when the index matters, and while/do when repetition is driven by a condition.

topics.challenge: Create a List<string> with at least three values, add another value, and print them with foreach.
topics.hint: List<T> needs a type argument between angle brackets, such as List<string>.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#

topics.title: Methods, Parameters & Return Values
topics.summary: Package behavior into methods with clear inputs/outputs and learn optional, named, ref/out, and expression-bodied forms gradually.

concepts.name: Method signature
concepts.explanation: A method declares accessibility/modifiers, return type, name, and parameters. The parameter types are part of overload selection.

concepts.name: Return values
concepts.explanation: Use void when no value is returned; otherwise every reachable path must satisfy the method return contract unless execution throws.

concepts.name: Parameters
concepts.explanation: Arguments are passed by value by default. ref, out, and in change parameter passing semantics and should be used only when their intent is clear.

topics.challenge: Write one method that accepts two numeric parameters and returns a calculated result, then call it.
topics.hint: Choose a non-void return type and return the computed value instead of only printing inside the method.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#

topics.title: Classes, Objects & Basic Encapsulation
topics.summary: Create your own reference types with fields/properties, constructors, methods, and controlled access to state.

concepts.name: Class and instance
concepts.explanation: A class describes a type; new creates an instance. Each instance has its own instance state while static members belong to the type itself.

concepts.name: Properties
concepts.explanation: Properties expose get/set accessors and are the normal public data surface for C# objects. Auto-properties are concise when no custom accessor logic is required.

concepts.name: Constructors
concepts.explanation: Constructors establish valid initial state. Prefer objects that cannot exist in obviously invalid states after construction.

topics.challenge: Create a class with two properties, a constructor, and one method that changes controlled state.
topics.hint: Use private set when callers should be able to read a property but not assign it directly.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#
